summary: Induction on m. A chain value at stage m + 1 is a class integral over stage m; by joint invariance the integrand is right K_m-invariant, by the induction hypothesis its values lie in the smaller sumset, and with free stabilisers the integral is a sum over the classes.

steps.claim: Choose, for every stage j, form φ and point g, a linear map B_j(φ, g) with chain(k, Φ, j)(φ)(g) = B_j(φ, g)(⊗Φ) for all data Φ (exists_linear_chain_eq_pure).
steps.lean: choose B hb using exists_linear_chain_eq_pure k

induction' m with j ih; simpa [← hb, *] using hL (B 0 φ h)
  let T g β : TensorChain S j.succ →ₗ[ℂ] _ :=
    TensorProduct.lift ((k j).jetMatrix.compl₁₂ ((k j).ω (g, h)) β)
  have (g) β f : T g β (TensorChain.pure f _) = _ := TensorProduct.lift.tmul _ (TensorChain.pure ..)
  erw [Finset.prod_range_succ, mul_nsmul, ← classIntegral_sum _ (L · |>.toAddMonoidHom) (fun _ ↦ 1)
    (by simp) (by tauto)]
  refine classIntegral_mem_nsmul ?_ (fun a ha g ↦ ?_) fun _ ↦ ih (L := (L · ∘ₗ _)) (fun a _ β ↦ by
    simpa [*] using H a (by bound) (T ..)) ?_ ?_ fun β _ ↦ hL (T ..) ?_ <;> try tauto
  simpa [*, ← hb, ↓chain_equivariant] using
    H (Pi.mulSingle j ⟨a, ha⟩) (by simp_all [ne_of_gt]) (T g (B j φ g))

steps.claim: m = 0: the chain is the identity, the sum is ∑_x L_x(φ(h)) = ∑_x L_x(B_0(φ, h)(1)), which lies in A by hL (with hB for the property), and the empty product of class numbers is 1.
steps.lean: simpa [← hb, *] using hL (B 0 φ h)

steps.claim: m = j + 1, with induction hypothesis ih for j.
steps.lean:
let T g β : TensorChain S j.succ →ₗ[ℂ] _ :=
    TensorProduct.lift ((k j).jetMatrix.compl₁₂ ((k j).ω (g, h)) β)
  have (g) β f : T g β (TensorChain.pure f _) = _ := TensorProduct.lift.tmul _ (TensorChain.pure ..)
  erw [Finset.prod_range_succ, mul_nsmul, ← classIntegral_sum _ (L · |>.toAddMonoidHom) (fun _ ↦ 1)
    (by simp) (by tauto)]
  refine classIntegral_mem_nsmul ?_ (fun a ha g ↦ ?_) fun _ ↦ ih (L := (L · ∘ₗ _)) (fun a _ β ↦ by
    simpa [*] using H a (by bound) (T ..)) ?_ ?_ fun β _ ↦ hL (T ..) ?_ <;> try tauto
  simpa [*, ← hb, ↓chain_equivariant] using
    H (Pi.mulSingle j ⟨a, ha⟩) (by simp_all [ne_of_gt]) (T g (B j φ g))

steps.claim: For a point g and a linear map β, let T(g, β) be the linear map on S_j ⊗ (S_{j−1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ S_0) sending s ⊗ t to the value of the j-th jet matrix of ω_j(g, h)s on β(t).
steps.lean:
let T g β : TensorChain S j.succ →ₗ[ℂ] _ :=
    TensorProduct.lift ((k j).jetMatrix.compl₁₂ ((k j).ω (g, h)) β)

steps.claim: T(g, β) on a pure tensor f_j ⊗ (pure tensor of f) is given by this formula (TensorProduct.lift.tmul).
steps.lean: have (g) β f : T g β (TensorChain.pure f _) = _ := TensorProduct.lift.tmul _ (TensorChain.pure ..)

steps.claim: The chain value at stage j + 1 is the class integral over the classes of stage j of g ↦ jetMatrix_j(ω_j(g, h)Φ_{x,j})(chain(k, Φ_x, j)(φ)(g)) (Kernel.lift); so ∑_x L_x(…) is the class integral of g ↦ ∑_x L_x(…) (classIntegral_sum), and ∏_{j′<j+1} = (∏_{j′<j})·|classes_j| (prod_range_succ, mul_nsmul).

By classIntegral_mem_nsmul (free stabilisers, fr), it suffices that the integrand is right K_j-invariant and that its values lie in (∏_{j′<j} |classes|)·A; the latter is the induction hypothesis for the maps L_x ∘ T(g, ·): joint invariance at stage j is H with a_j = 1, and the propagation hypotheses come from hs.
steps.lean:
refine classIntegral_mem_nsmul ?_ (fun a ha g ↦ ?_) fun _ ↦ ih (L := (L · ∘ₗ _)) (fun a _ β ↦ by
    simpa [*] using H a (by bound) (T ..)) ?_ ?_ fun β _ ↦ hL (T ..) ?_ <;> try tauto

steps.claim: Right K_j-invariance: for a ∈ K_j, joint invariance H for the family with a at j and 1 elsewhere, together with chain_equivariant, shows that translating g by a leaves the integrand unchanged.
steps.lean:
simpa [*, ← hb, ↓chain_equivariant] using
    H (Pi.mulSingle j ⟨a, ha⟩) (by simp_all [ne_of_gt]) (T g (B j φ g))
